title: Visual daily routine
examples: Teacher, what do we do after playtime?
Can you show me the order of our day?
What happens between snack time and circle time?

explain.say: Today we talk about our daily routine. Our routine helps us know what comes next. We use boards to see the order of things.
Now look! Here it is in 3D: a calm bedroom at bedtime. Can you see the bed and the lamp? Tap any part, and I will tell you about it.
Look at this board. It shows what we do first. First we might sing a welcome song. Then we do something else.
This is called a first then board. It shows the order of two activities. For example, first we wash hands, then we eat lunch.
Transitions are moving from one thing to another. Moving from play to quiet time is a transition. We need to know what to do next.
When you get home from school, you first put your backpack down. Then you wash your hands with soap. This shows the order of your arrival.

draw.text: First: Put down bag, Then: Wash hands

faq.a: A routine is a regular pattern of activities that happen every day. It helps us feel safe and know what to expect.

faq.q: What do first then boards show?
faq.a: They show the order of two things happening one after the other. It tells us what comes right after the first thing.
asks: How do I use the first then board?

faq.a: A transition is the time we move from one activity to the next. It helps us change our focus gently.
asks: How do we move from one thing to another?

faq.q: If we finish playtime, what comes next?
faq.a: You should look at our routine board. It will show the next activity we need to do together.
asks: Where can I see what is next?

faq.q: Do we always do things in the same order?
faq.a: Most days we do things in the same order. This helps our brains know what to expect every day.
asks: Is our day always the same?
Does the schedule always stay the same?

facts: A routine helps children feel calm and secure.
First then boards show a clear sequence of two events.
Transitions help us move smoothly between different activities.
Knowing the schedule helps us prepare for what comes next.

quiz.say: If the board shows 'Circle Time $\rightarrow$ Story Time', what happens after Circle Time?
quiz.why: The arrow shows that Story Time comes right after Circle Time.

wrong.1: Playtime is usually before Circle Time, not after.
wrong.2: Snack Time might happen later, but the board shows Story Time next.
wrong.3: Outside Play is a different activity and not shown next.

quiz.say: What word describes moving from painting to reading books?
quiz.why: Moving from one activity to another is called a transition.

wrong.0: Routine is the whole pattern, not just the moving part.
wrong.1: First only tells us the beginning, not the change.
wrong.2: Then only tells us what comes second, not the action of changing.

quiz.say: If the board shows 'Wash Hands $\rightarrow$ Lunch', what is the correct order?
quiz.why: The arrow shows you must wash your hands before you can have lunch.

wrong.0: You must clean your hands before you eat your lunch.
wrong.1: You need to do one thing, and then do the next thing.
wrong.2: The board shows a specific order you must follow.
